nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a canonical bitstring encoding. For every $a \in \alpha$, decoding the bitstring encoding of $a$ succeeds and returns $a$.
nodes.title: Decoding inverts bitstring encoding

nodes.summary: For a type $\alpha$ with a canonical bitstring encoding, bitstring decoding is the decoding function of that encoding: it sends each finite list of booleans either to an element of $\alpha$ or to failure.
nodes.title: Decoding function of a bitstring encoding

nodes.summary: For a type $\alpha$ with a canonical bitstring encoding, the bitstring encoding of $a \in \alpha$ is the finite list of booleans that this encoding assigns to $a$.
nodes.title: Encoding function of a bitstring encoding

nodes.summary: A canonical bitstring encoding of a type $\alpha$ consists of an encoding map from $\alpha$ to finite lists of booleans and a partial decoding map from finite lists of booleans to $\alpha$, such that decoding the encoding of any $a \in \alpha$ succeeds and returns $a$.
nodes.title: Bitstring encodings

nodes.summary: The class coNP. coNP is the set of decision problems $L$ whose complement, the decision problem that accepts exactly the bitstrings that $L$ rejects, belongs to NP.
nodes.title: The class coNP

nodes.summary: A complexity class is a set of decision problems.
nodes.title: Complexity classes

nodes.summary: A decision problem is a function from finite lists of booleans (bitstrings) to booleans.
nodes.title: Decision problems

nodes.summary: The self-delimiting form of a bitstring $(b_1, \dots, b_n)$ is $(\mathrm{true}, b_1, \dots, \mathrm{true}, b_n, \mathrm{false})$: each bit is preceded by $\mathrm{true}$ and the block is terminated by $\mathrm{false}$. In particular the empty bitstring becomes $(\mathrm{false})$.
nodes.title: Self-delimiting form of a bitstring

nodes.summary: Let $e_\alpha$ encode $\alpha$ as words over an alphabet $\Gamma_\alpha$ and $e_\beta$ encode $\beta$ as words over $\Gamma_\beta$. A function $f : \alpha \to \beta$ is polynomial-time computable with respect to $e_\alpha$ and $e_\beta$ when there are a multi-stack Turing machine with finitely many stacks, function labels and internal states and a finite input stack alphabet, identifications of its input and output…
nodes.title: Polynomial-time computability under given encodings

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be types with canonical bitstring encodings. A function $f : \alpha \to \beta$ is polynomial-time computable when it is polynomial-time computable with respect to the canonical bitstring encodings of $\alpha$ and $\beta$.
nodes.title: Polynomial-time computable functions

nodes.summary: NP is the set of decision problems $L$ (functions from lists of booleans to booleans) for which there exist a polynomial $p$ with natural-number coefficients and a polynomial-time computable function $R$ from pairs of lists of booleans to booleans such that, for every list of booleans $x$, $L(x)$ is true if and only if there is a list of booleans $w$ whose length is at most $p$ evaluated at the length of $x$ and…
nodes.title: The complexity class NP

nodes.summary: P is the set of decision problems (functions from lists of booleans to booleans) that are computable in polynomial time by a deterministic multi-stack Turing machine, with respect to the canonical bitstring encodings of inputs and outputs.
nodes.title: The complexity class P

nodes.summary: Given a bound $n$ and a list of booleans $s$, the parse returns the empty list of payloads if $s$ is empty. If $s$ is nonempty and $n = 0$ it fails. If $s$ is nonempty and $n = m + 1$, it parses one self-delimiting block from the front of $s$, then parses the remaining list with bound $m$, and returns the first payload followed by the payloads of the rest. It fails if either step fails. So the parse succeeds…
nodes.title: Bounded parsing of self-delimiting blocks

nodes.summary: Given a list of booleans $s$, this repeatedly parses one self-delimiting block from the front of $s$ until $s$ is used up, allowing at most as many blocks as the length of $s$, and returns the list of payloads in order. It fails if some block fails to parse. The bound never binds, since every block uses at least one bit. So the parse succeeds exactly when $s$ is a concatenation of self-delimiting blocks.
nodes.title: Parsing a list of booleans into self-delimiting blocks

nodes.summary: Write booleans as bits, with true as $1$ and false as $0$. Reading a list of bits from the front, a $0$ ends the block, and a $1$ followed by a bit $b$ contributes $b$ to the payload. The result is the payload together with the rest of the list after the terminating $0$. Parsing fails if the list runs out before a terminating $0$ is read.
nodes.title: Parsing one self-delimiting block

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
